title: Eggs Fried with Garlic and Mint (Beid Ma’li ma‘ Toom)
steps: Crush the garlic with a little salt and stir in the lemon juice.
prep
Fry the garlic mixture briefly in the oil.
Slide the eggs into the pan and fry them, spooning the hot garlicky oil over them once or twice.
Sprinkle with the mint, salt and pepper and serve.
finish

title: Eggs Fried with Lemon Juice (Beid Ma’li ma‘ Lamun)
steps: Heat the oil until it sizzles and slide in the eggs.
Pour the lemon juice over them straight away.
Baste the eggs with the pan juices once or twice as they set.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
finish

title: Eggs with Pastirma (Beid Ma’li bi-l-Bastirma)
steps: Trim away the tough spiced rind of the pastirma.
prep
Put the pastirma in the pan with the cold oil and heat them together, since pastirma crisps within moments once hot.
Turn the slices so both sides cook, then add the eggs, whole or beaten.
As soon as the eggs have set, slide everything onto a plate and season.
finish
Take care not to overcook the pastirma; it turns bitter.
finish

title: Eggs with Tomato and Onion (Beid Ma’li bi-l-Tamatim)
steps: Chop the onion very finely. Peel the tomatoes and cut them into slices about 1 cm thick.
prep
Soften the onion in the oil, then add the tomatoes and cook for 10–12 minutes.
Break the eggs over the tomato and onion and cook until set.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
finish

Alexandrian style (Shakshukat Beid Iskandarani, recipe 46 in the book): use shelled hard-boiled eggs instead of raw ones. Slide them in whole and cook for 5 minutes, then halve them, arrange them on a dish and spoon the tomato mixture over.
alternative

title: Fried Hard-Boiled Eggs with Cumin (Beid Miza’lil)
steps: Peel the eggs, keeping them whole.
prep
Fry them in very hot oil, rolling them around until browned on every side.
Serve on a bed of parsley, sprinkled with cumin, salt and pepper.
finish

title: Egg and Yogurt Sandwich Spread (Beid bi-l-Zabadi)
steps: Peel the eggs and mash them with a fork.
Mix in the yogurt, mustard, salt and pepper.
Spread on bread for sandwiches.
finish

title: Herb and Sumac Omelet (‘Igga bi-l-Tawabil)
steps: Beat the eggs with the sifted flour, herbs, spices, salt and pepper.
prep
Fry the finely chopped onion in the oil until pale gold, then pour in the eggs over a high heat.
As the bottom sets, tilt the pan or lift the edge so the runny egg flows underneath.
Turn the omelet and fry until both sides are golden and dry.
finish
notes: A spiced take on the everyday Egyptian ‘igga, a flat omelet fried firm on both sides.

title: Stuffed Omelet with Five Fillings (‘Igga Mahshiya)
ingredients: Filling A: boiled gizzards, diced very small
Filling B: fried kidneys, diced very small
Filling C: fried liver, diced very small
steps: Prepare one of the fillings and keep it warm.
prep
Beat the eggs, add the sifted flour, salt and pepper and beat again.
Fry the very finely chopped onion in the oil until pale gold, pour in the eggs and cook over a high heat.
When the underside sets, tilt the pan or lift the edge so the liquid egg runs underneath.
Turn the omelet over and spoon the filling down the middle.
Fold the edges over the filling and serve.
finish

title: Dukkah Spice and Nut Dip (Du’’a)
steps: Grind all the ingredients together in a mortar or a blender.
Eat by dipping pieces of baladi bread into the mixture.
finish
notes: Use any cup or spoon as the “measure”, keeping the proportions.

title: Homemade Labneh (Labna)
steps: Stir the salt into the yogurt.
prep
Pour it into a wet cheesecloth bag, tie the top and hang it for 24 hours over a clean bowl.
Keep the whey that drips out; it is nourishing and can be drunk or used in cooking.
Spoon the labneh into a jar and pour a little oil, preferably olive oil, over the top.
finish

Labneh balls for keeping: hang a larger batch for longer, opening the bag every 24 hours to stir the yogurt (it thickens faster near the cloth) and adding a little more salt each day. When it is thick and even all through, roll small amounts into balls with wet hands and keep them in a jar half full of olive oil.
alternative
notes: Labneh comes from the Levant (Palestine, Lebanon, Syria and Jordan). It was traditionally made from goat’s milk, which gives it a pleasant sourness, but buffalo or cow’s milk yogurt works just as well. The soft, spoonable kind is called labneh khadra.

title: Homemade Pastirma (Bastirma)
ingredients: Beef fillet or another prime cut
steps: Trim every bit of fat from the meat, dry it well and make two or three very shallow cuts in the surface.
prep
Roll the meat in 1/4 cup of the salt so it is completely covered.
Lay it on a rack with a weight on top so the juices drain away, and leave it for 3–4 days.
Take off the weight, wipe the meat dry and thread a cord through one end, leaving a long loop for hanging.
Peel and crush the garlic and knead it with the fenugreek, chili and the rest of the salt into a soft paste.
Coat the meat with the paste in a layer 1/2–1 cm thick.
Hang it for another 3–4 days, until it is thoroughly dry and dark brown.
Slice paper-thin and eat it raw at breakfast, with or without the rind, or fry it with eggs or use it in pastries.
finish
notes: Most families buy pastirma, but it is easy to make at home. When cooking it, heat it together with the oil rather than dropping it into hot fat: it crisps almost at once and turns bitter if overcooked.

title: Sweet Vermicelli with Raisins (Sha‘riya)
steps: Break the vermicelli with your fingers into pieces 2–3 cm long.
prep
Fry the raisins lightly in the oil until they puff up, then lift them out.
Fry the vermicelli in the same oil until pale brown.
Dissolve the sugar in the boiling water and pour it over the vermicelli, add the raisins, and cook over a low heat for about 15 minutes.
If the water is absorbed before the vermicelli is tender, sprinkle in a little more hot water.
Serve with warm milk poured over each plate.
finish
For a buffet dessert, add chopped bananas, strawberries and mixed nuts.
alternative
notes: A breakfast dish for festive mornings, also served among the sweets at open buffets.

title: Eggs with Fried White Cheese (Beid Ma’li ma‘ Jibneh Beida)
ingredients: Hard white cheese, in 1 cm slices
steps: Fry the cheese one slice at a time, turning it to colour both sides, and keep it warm at the side of the serving dish.
Fry the eggs in the same oil, basting them as they cook.
Serve the eggs next to the fried cheese, sprinkled with salt and pepper.
finish
notes: A breakfast dish from Palestine, Lebanon and Jordan.

title: Yemeni Fatut with Fenugreek (Fatut bi-l-Hulba)
steps: Blend the fenugreek, tomato paste and zhug into a paste.
prep
Tear the bread into bite-sized pieces and fry them in the ghee until crisp.
Add the eggs to the pan and stir until they are well set and scrambled with the bread.
Boil the chicken stock with the fenugreek paste, uncovered and over a high heat, until reduced by half.
Add the egg and bread mixture and cook for 3–5 minutes more, then season.
Serve with a little lemon juice added to each plate.
finish
notes: A Yemeni breakfast. Zhug is in this collection too, among the pastes and spice mixtures.

title: Turkish Eggs on Spinach and Feta (Ispanaklı Yumurta)
steps: Wash the spinach in several changes of water, drain it in a colander and shred it coarsely.
prep
Fry the onion in the oil until it softens.
Add the spinach and stir over a medium heat until the leaves wilt and release their liquid.
Turn up the heat and cook until only enough liquid is left to cover the bottom of the pan.
Stir in the crumbled cheese, salt and pepper.
Break the eggs onto the spinach, spacing them evenly, cover the pan and cook over a medium heat until the eggs are set.
Serve straight from the pan.
finish

title: Turkish Poached Eggs in Garlic Yogurt (Çılbır)
steps: Mix the yogurt with the garlic, salt and pepper and warm it in an ovenproof dish in a moderately hot oven.
Meanwhile, poach the eggs in simmering water with the vinegar and, once set, lay them on the yogurt.
Melt the butter, stir in the paprika and drizzle the red butter over the eggs.
Return the dish to the oven for 2–3 minutes, then serve on individual plates and season to taste.
finish

title: Lebanese Baked Eggs in Yogurt (Beid bi-l-Laban)
steps: Whisk the egg white until stiff and stir it into the yogurt; this keeps the yogurt from splitting.
prep
Cook the yogurt uncovered over a very low heat for 5–7 minutes, then pour it into a shallow ovenproof dish.
Fry the garlic in the ghee until golden, stirring all the time so it does not stick, then stir in the mint, salt and pepper.
Break the eggs over the yogurt, spacing them evenly, and pour the garlic ghee over them.
Bake until the eggs are set.
finish

title: Tunisian Ojja with Merguez and Potatoes (Ojja bi Mergaz)
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and diced very small
steps: Pound the garlic with salt, the paprika and the caraway.
prep
Sauté the potatoes in the oil, then add the tomato paste, the garlic mixture, the harissa and just enough water to cover.
Cook over a low heat for 15 minutes.
Add the sausages and cook for another 15 minutes.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper, pour them over the stew and stir.
Serve as soon as the eggs are set.
finish
notes: A Tunisian dish; ojja is the Tunisian cousin of shakshuka.

title: Brain Omelet (Ijjit Nukha’aat)
steps: Parboil the brain in salted water, drain it, remove the veins and mash it.
prep
Soften the onion in ghee, add the garlic and fry until golden, stirring all the time, then take the pan off the heat.
Beat the eggs and stir in the brain, the onion and garlic, the lemon juice, parsley, salt and pepper.
Heat more ghee and pour in the egg mixture. As the bottom sets, lift the edge so the runny egg flows underneath.
Turn the omelet and fry until both sides are golden and set.
Cut into thick wedges and serve.
finish
notes: Made in Lebanon, Syria and Jordan.

title: Persian Eggplant Kuku (Kuku-ye Bademjan)
steps: Peel and dice the eggplants, sprinkle them with salt and leave for an hour.
prep
Squeeze them dry, fry until golden, then mash them in a deep bowl.
Beat in the eggs, onion, cumin, salt and pepper until smooth.
Heat ghee in a pan and pour in the mixture. As the bottom sets, lift the edge so the uncooked egg runs underneath.
Turn the kuku over and fry until both sides are brown.
Cut into thick wedges and serve with yogurt spooned over each plate.
finish

title: Persian Potato Kuku or Patties (Kuku-ye Sibzamini)
steps: Peel and boil the potatoes, then mash them in a deep bowl.
prep
Mix in the eggs, onion, turmeric, salt and pepper until smooth.
Heat ghee and fry the mixture like a thick omelet, lifting the edge as the bottom sets so the uncooked egg runs underneath.
Turn it over and fry until brown on both sides.
Cut into thick wedges and serve.
finish
Patties: drop spoonfuls of the mixture into hot ghee, flatten them and deep-fry, then drain on absorbent paper.
alternative
